prompt: Write a JavaScript function rotate(arr, k) that returns a new array with the elements of arr rotated right by k positions. k is a non-negative integer and may be larger than arr.length. An empty array returns an empty array.

Write a JavaScript function isBalanced(s) that returns true if the brackets in the string s are correctly balanced and nested, false otherwise. It must handle (), [] and {}. Characters other than brackets are ignored. An empty string is balanced.
Write a JavaScript function romanToInt(s) that converts an uppercase Roman numeral string (values 1 to 3999) into its integer value, handling subtractive pairs such as IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM.

Write a JavaScript function longestCommonPrefix(strs) that returns the longest common prefix string of an array of strings, or an empty string if there is none. An empty array returns an empty string.

Write a JavaScript function mergeIntervals(intervals) that takes an array of [start, end] pairs, merges every overlapping or touching pair, and returns the merged intervals sorted by start. The input is not necessarily sorted. An empty array returns an empty array.
Write a JavaScript function flattenDeep(arr) that fully flattens an arbitrarily nested array into a single-level array, preserving order.

Write a JavaScript function chunk(arr, size) that splits arr into consecutive sub-arrays of length size, with the final chunk holding the remainder. size is a positive integer. An empty array returns an empty array.
Write a JavaScript function binarySearch(sorted, target) that returns the index of target in the ascending-sorted array sorted using binary search, or -1 if it is absent.

Write a JavaScript function wordFrequencies(text) that returns a plain object mapping each lowercased word in text to how many times it occurs. Words are runs of letters and digits; punctuation separates words. Empty text returns an empty object.

Write a JavaScript function deepEqual(a, b) that returns true when a and b are structurally equal, recursing through plain objects and arrays and comparing other values with ===. Key order must not matter.

Write a JavaScript function camelCase(str) that converts a string written with spaces, hyphens or underscores into camelCase: first word lowercase, each later word capitalised, separators removed. An empty string returns an empty string.
Write a JavaScript function spiralOrder(matrix) that returns the elements of a rectangular 2D array in clockwise spiral order starting at the top-left. An empty matrix returns an empty array.
Write a JavaScript function lengthOfLongestSubstring(s) that returns the length of the longest substring of s containing no repeated character. An empty string returns 0.
Write a JavaScript function maxSubArray(nums) that returns the largest sum obtainable from a contiguous non-empty subarray of nums. nums may be entirely negative.

Write a JavaScript function coinChange(coins, amount) that returns the fewest coins needed to make amount from unlimited coins of the given denominations, or -1 if it cannot be made. amount 0 needs 0 coins.
Write a JavaScript function intToRoman(num) that converts an integer from 1 to 3999 into its Roman numeral string, using the subtractive forms IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM.

Write a JavaScript function rleCompress(s) that run-length encodes s, so each run of a character becomes the character followed by its count. Return the encoded string only when it is strictly shorter than the input; otherwise return the input unchanged.
Write a JavaScript function evalRPN(tokens) that evaluates an array of reverse Polish notation tokens using +, -, * and /, where division truncates toward zero. Returns an integer.

Write a JavaScript function numDecodings(s) that counts how many ways the digit string s decodes to letters, where 1 maps to A through 26 maps to Z. A leading zero in any group makes that grouping invalid, so a string that cannot be decoded returns 0.

Write a JavaScript function longestPalindrome(s) that returns the longest palindromic substring of s. If several tie for longest, return the one that starts earliest. An empty string returns an empty string.
